strategies.title: The golden cross
strategies.claim: Buy when the 50-day average crosses above the 200-day; sell when it crosses back.
strategies.lesson: Slow averages cross rarely, so even twenty years of daily prices give only a handful of trades: too few to tell an edge from luck, however good the total looks.
strategies.text: Buy when crosses_above(sma(50), sma(200)); get out when crosses_below(sma(50), sma(200)).

strategies.title: Above the 200-day average
strategies.claim: Own it only while the price is above its 200-day average.
strategies.lesson: A trend filter changes when you are in the market more than how much each trade makes. It can skip the worst falls and still trail simply holding, because it also misses part of every rebound.
strategies.text: Buy when close > sma(200); get out when close < sma(200).

strategies.title: RSI 30/70
strategies.claim: Buy when the 14-day RSI drops under 30 (oversold); sell above 70 (overbought).
strategies.lesson: In a rising market the daily RSI seldom reaches 30, so the rule waits a long time and sits out most of the rise. Few trades again, and a long wait between them.
strategies.text: Buy when rsi(14) < 30; get out when rsi(14) > 70.

strategies.title: RSI(2) dip in an uptrend
strategies.claim: In an uptrend (above the 200-day average), buy a 2-day RSI under 10; sell when the price closes above its 5-day average.
strategies.lesson: Short dips in an uptrend are a pattern traders have known for decades. Once a pattern is famous, the question is whether anything is left after costs, and many trades make costs add up.
strategies.text: Buy when rsi(2) < 10 and close > sma(200); get out when close > sma(5).

strategies.title: Bollinger band bounce
strategies.claim: Buy two standard deviations under the 20-day average; sell back at the average.
strategies.lesson: Buying far under the average is a bet that prices snap back. In a market that keeps falling they don't, and those few trades decide the result.
strategies.text: Buy when close < sma(20) - 2 * std(20); get out when close > sma(20).

strategies.title: MACD cross
strategies.claim: Buy when the MACD line (12/26) crosses above its 9-day signal line; sell when it crosses below.
strategies.lesson: MACD is a moving-average cross in disguise. It trades often, every trade pays costs, and an edge has to beat all of them.
strategies.text: Buy when crosses_above(ema(12) - ema(26), ema(ema(12) - ema(26), 9)); get out when crosses_below(ema(12) - ema(26), ema(ema(12) - ema(26), 9)).

strategies.title: EMA 9/21 cross
strategies.claim: Buy when the 9-day EMA crosses above the 21-day EMA; sell when it crosses below.
strategies.lesson: Fast crosses trade often. Each extra trade is another cost and another chance for luck, so a big total on one market says little until the trades clear the bar.
strategies.text: Buy when crosses_above(ema(9), ema(21)); get out when crosses_below(ema(9), ema(21)).

strategies.title: 20-day breakout
strategies.claim: Buy a close above the highest close of the last 20 days; sell under the lowest of the last 10.
strategies.lesson: Breakouts are the classic trend-following entry: they win big rarely and lose small often, so the result hangs on a few trades, and a short record says little.
strategies.text: Buy when close > prev(highest(20)); get out when close < prev(lowest(10)).

strategies.title: Buy a 5% dip
strategies.claim: Buy after a 5% drop in five days; sell ten days later.
strategies.lesson: Buying a drop works until the drop keeps going. A few large losses decide the result, which is why the judge raises the bar for records whose losses are rarer but bigger.
strategies.text: Buy when pct(5) < -5; get out after 10 bars.

strategies.title: 5% under the 20-day average
strategies.claim: Buy when the price is 5% under its 20-day average; sell back at the average.
strategies.lesson: A rule that waits for big gaps trades rarely in calm markets and too early in a crash: it has few trades to judge and its worst ones come together.
strategies.text: Buy when close < sma(20) * 0.95; get out when close > sma(20).
